audit_items.title: Do specific EIP-7883 test vectors produce expected gas costs?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): EIP-7883 ModExp gas pricing is implemented in execution layer clients (Geth, Reth, etc.), not in Prysm which is a consensus layer client. No ModExp precompile implementation exists in this codebase.

code_scope.resolution: EL-specific EVM precompile not present in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-7825 gas cap activated only at Fusaka fork block?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): EIP-7825 block gas limit cap (16777216) is enforced at the execution layer during block validation. Prysm is a consensus layer client and does not implement EL block gas limit validation.

code_scope.resolution: EL-specific block gas limit validation not present in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-7883 ModExp formula activated only at Fusaka fork block?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): EIP-7883 ModExp formula fork activation is handled by execution layer clients. Prysm is a consensus layer client with no ModExp precompile or EIP-7883 fork logic.

code_scope.resolution: EL-specific precompile fork activation not present in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-024: Do corrupted withdrawal instructions from the consensus layer fail validation before crediting amounts?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): Withdrawal crediting and withdrawals_root validation against withdrawal lists is performed by the execution layer client. Prysm (CL) provides withdrawals to the EL via Engine API but does not perform EL-side validation of withdrawal crediting. The CL produces withdrawal instructions; the EL validates and credits them.

code_scope.resolution: EL-side withdrawal crediting validation not present in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Execution Client Independent Verification: Does the execution client independently verify withdrawals_root before crediting balances?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): This check explicitly targets 'execution client' verification of withdrawals_root and balance crediting. Prysm is a consensus layer client. The execution client (Geth, Reth, etc.) is responsible for computing and validating withdrawals_root.

code_scope.resolution: Execution client withdrawal verification not present in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-024: Can an attacker inject fabricated withdrawal instructions not authorized by the beacon chain via the Engine API?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): This check targets EL-side Engine API validation of withdrawal instructions and JWT enforcement. While Prysm sends withdrawal data via Engine API, the receiving validation (JWT auth, beacon root verification on the EL side) is implemented in the execution client, not the consensus client.

code_scope.resolution: EL-side Engine API withdrawal injection prevention not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify JWT Authentication Enforcement: Is the Engine API JWT authentication properly implemented to prevent unauthorized access?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): JWT authentication enforcement on the Engine API server side is implemented in the execution client. While Prysm (CL) uses JWT to authenticate as a client, the check targets server-side JWT validation (token expiry, algorithm confusion, secret management) which is in the EL.

code_scope.resolution: EL-side JWT server authentication not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Beacon Block Root Cryptographic Anchor: Does the parent_beacon_block_root provide sufficient cryptographic assurance?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): This check targets the execution client's validation of parent_beacon_block_root against its view of the canonical beacon chain, and withdrawal merkle proof verification. These are EL-side validations performed when processing Engine API payloads.

code_scope.resolution: EL-side beacon block root validation not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-025: Are excessive log emissions properly bounded by gas limits to prevent bloom filter DoS?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): Bloom filter construction from transaction logs and LOG opcode gas metering are EVM execution layer concepts. Prysm (CL) does not process EVM logs, construct bloom filters, or meter LOG opcode gas costs.

code_scope.resolution: EVM bloom filter and LOG opcode processing not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify EVM LOG opcode gas metering correctly accounts for bloom filter processing overhead
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): EVM LOG0-LOG4 opcode implementation and gas metering are execution layer responsibilities. Prysm (CL) does not implement EVM opcodes or gas metering.

code_scope.resolution: EVM opcode gas metering not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-022: Are transaction fields (gas, value, data, to, nonce) protected from modification in transit?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): Transaction ECDSA signature verification and transaction field integrity checking are performed by the execution layer client's transaction pool. Prysm (CL) does not process individual Ethereum transactions or verify ECDSA transaction signatures.

code_scope.resolution: EL transaction signature verification not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Execution Client Transaction Validation: Does the execution client correctly reject transactions with invalid ECDSA signatures?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): This check explicitly targets 'execution client' ECDSA signature verification. Prysm is a consensus layer client that uses BLS signatures for beacon chain operations, not ECDSA for Ethereum transactions.

code_scope.resolution: Execution client ECDSA verification not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are EIP-7702 SetCodeTransaction authorization signatures individually validated with proper ECDSA verification?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): EIP-7702 SetCodeTransaction is an EL transaction type. Authorization tuple processing, ECDSA verification, and code delegation are implemented in the execution engine. No EIP-7702 or SetCodeTransaction references exist in the Prysm codebase.

code_scope.resolution: EIP-7702 SetCodeTransaction not implemented in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Does the execution engine enforce chain_id validation in EIP-7702 authorizations to prevent cross-chain replay attacks?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): EIP-7702 authorization chain_id validation is performed by the execution engine. Prysm (CL) does not process EIP-7702 transactions or validate EL-level chain_id in authorization tuples.

code_scope.resolution: EIP-7702 chain_id validation not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Is nonce validation properly enforced for EIP-7702 authorizations to prevent authorization replay attacks?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): EIP-7702 authorization nonce validation is an execution engine responsibility. Prysm (CL) does not track EL account nonces or process EIP-7702 authorization tuples.

code_scope.resolution: EIP-7702 nonce validation not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does encode_account maintain canonical RLP tuple ordering (nonce, balance, storage_root, code_hash)?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): RLP account encoding (nonce, balance, storage_root, code_hash) is an execution layer state trie operation. Prysm (CL) uses SSZ encoding for beacon state, not RLP for EL account state. No encode_account function exists in Prysm.

code_scope.resolution: RLP encode_account not in CL codebase (CL uses SSZ)

audit_items.title: Does the execution client reject transactions that would result in non-canonical account state encoding?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): This check explicitly targets 'execution client' transaction processing and state trie operations. Prysm is a consensus layer client that does not maintain EL account state or perform RLP encoding of accounts.

code_scope.resolution: EL state trie account encoding not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-016: Does parse_deposit_requests use exact equality (==) to compare log.address against DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): parse_deposit_requests is an EL function that filters EVM transaction logs by deposit contract address during block processing. While Prysm has DepositContractAddress in its config, the log filtering and address comparison logic (parse_deposit_requests) is implemented in the execution layer client.

code_scope.resolution: EL-side parse_deposit_requests log filtering not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify actor-execution-client correctly filters deposit events: Are all log sources validated before deposit event processing?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): This check explicitly targets 'actor-execution-client' deposit event filtering from EVM logs. Prysm (CL) receives processed deposit requests from the EL via execution payloads; it does not filter raw EVM logs.

code_scope.resolution: EL-side log event filtering not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-016: Does extract_deposit_data validate total data length is exactly 576 bytes before processing?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): extract_deposit_data is an EL function that parses raw deposit log data (576 bytes ABI-encoded format). Prysm (CL) receives deposit requests already parsed by the EL in SSZ format via execution payloads, not as raw 576-byte log data.

code_scope.resolution: EL-side extract_deposit_data not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-016: Are all five deposit field offsets validated against expected constants?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): Deposit field offset validation (PUBKEY_OFFSET=160, WC_OFFSET=256, etc.) is part of EL-side deposit log parsing. Prysm (CL) receives deposit requests in SSZ format, not as raw ABI-encoded data with offsets.

code_scope.resolution: EL-side deposit data offset validation not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-016: Are all five deposit field sizes (48, 32, 8, 96, 8 bytes) validated against expected constants?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): Deposit field size validation (pubkey=48, withdrawal_credentials=32, amount=8, signature=96, index=8) is part of EL-side deposit log data extraction. Prysm (CL) receives deposit requests in SSZ format from the execution payload.

code_scope.resolution: EL-side deposit field size validation not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-017: Does compute_requests_hash produce deterministic, identical output across all execution client implementations?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): compute_requests_hash is an EL function that produces a SHA-256 commitment over execution requests for block building. While Prysm has a RequestsHash field in its testing middleware, the actual hash computation and cross-client consistency is an EL responsibility.

code_scope.resolution: EL-side compute_requests_hash not implemented in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Execution Client SHA-256 Implementation: Is the SHA-256 algorithm correctly implemented with deterministic behavior?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): This check explicitly targets 'execution client' SHA-256 implementation for compute_requests_hash. While Prysm uses SHA-256 for other purposes, the specific execution request hashing context is EL-specific.

code_scope.resolution: EL-side SHA-256 request hashing implementation not in CL codebase

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-7702 authorization chain_id properly validated to prevent cross-chain replay attacks?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch (EL vs CL): EIP-7702 authorization chain_id validation is an execution layer concern. Prysm (CL) does not process EIP-7702 authorization tuples or validate EL transaction-level chain_id. No EIP-7702 references exist in the Prysm codebase.

code_scope.resolution: EIP-7702 chain_id validation not in CL codebase
